--- title: "[PolarsGAM]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} GAM that reads data from Polars LazyFrames, DataFrames, or files. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/polars_streaming.py#L89-L284){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python PolarsGAM(formula, family=None, *, n_discrete=200, chunk_size=100000) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `PolarsGAM` extends `~whittaker.bam.BigGAM` with a data-loading layer built on Polars, so it can source data from an in-memory Polars `DataFrame`/`LazyFrame` or directly from a file on disk (CSV, Parquet, IPC/Arrow, or NDJSON), without requiring the caller to materialize the whole dataset into a `dict` of NumPy arrays first. File paths are opened lazily (`pl.scan_*`), and the resulting `LazyFrame` is collected using Polars' streaming query engine (`collect(streaming=True)`), which evaluates the query plan incrementally rather than loading the entire source at once. The collected frame is then walked in `chunk_size`-row slices (`iter_slices`) and each column is converted to a NumPy array and concatenated, producing the same `dict[str, numpy.ndarray]` that `~whittaker.gam.GAM.fit` and `~whittaker.bam.BigGAM.fit` expect. Fitting itself then proceeds exactly as in `BigGAM`: covariates are discretized to at most `n_discrete` unique values per smooth, and the design matrix is never materialized. Use `PolarsGAM` when the data already lives in Polars, or on disk in a Polars-readable format, and you want to avoid a manual load-then-convert step — particularly for datasets in the 1M-100M row range where Polars' streaming engine keeps peak memory bounded during the read. For SQL-native sources or datasets that are more naturally expressed as a database query (joins, filters, aggregations), see `~whittaker.duckdb.DuckDBGAM` instead. Requires the `polars` package (install via `pip install whittaker[polars]`). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [formula]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str or Formula]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Model formula as a string (e.g. `"y ~ s(x1) + s(x2) + x3"`), or an already-parsed `Formula` object. Same syntax as `~whittaker.gam.GAM`. [family]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Family]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Response distribution family, e.g. `Gaussian()`, `Binomial()`, `Poisson()`, `Gamma()`, or `Tweedie()`. Defaults to `Gaussian()`. [n_discrete]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[200]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of unique representative values per covariate used when discretizing smooth terms (see `~whittaker.bam.BigGAM`). Defaults to `200`. [chunk_size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100000]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of rows collected per slice when converting the source into NumPy arrays. Smaller values reduce peak memory during the Polars-to-NumPy conversion step at the cost of more Python-level overhead; larger values reduce overhead but require more memory per slice. Defaults to `100_000`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#8adc4508 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import polars as pl from whittaker.polars_streaming import PolarsGAM rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 5_000 x1 = rng.uniform(0, 1, n) x2 = rng.uniform(0, 1, n) y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x1) + x2**2 + rng.normal(scale=0.2, size=n) df = pl.DataFrame({"x1": x1, "x2": x2, "y": y}) model = PolarsGAM("y ~ s(x1) + s(x2)", n_discrete=100, chunk_size=1_000) model.fit(df.lazy()) print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAM fit summary ============================================================ Formula: y ~ s(x1) + s(x2) Family: Gaussian(link='identity') Observations: 0 Coefficients: 19 Parametric coefficients: Term Estimate Std.Err t value p-value ------------------------ ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- (Intercept) 0.3353 0.0000 0.000 1 Approximate significance of smooth terms: Term EDF Ref.df Chi.sq p-value ------------------------ ------ ------ ---------- ---------- s(x1) 8.91 9 62252.794 < 1e-16 s(x2) 6.25 7 11058.710 < 1e-16 Total EDF: 16.16 Deviance: 199.7026 Null dev: 3148.4427 Dev. expl: 93.7% GCV score: 0.040200 Scale est: 0.040070 AIC: -1880.09 BIC: -1774.79 ``` ::: ::: A file path can be passed directly instead of a `DataFrame`/`LazyFrame` — `PolarsGAM` infers the format from the extension and scans it lazily: ::: {#ff8d700e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} model = PolarsGAM("y ~ s(x)") model.fit("large_dataset.parquet") ``` ::: Fitting from an actual multi-gigabyte file requires `pip install whittaker[polars]` and enough disk I/O bandwidth to stream the file; the in-memory example above is kept small so it runs quickly, but the same code path scales to files with tens of millions of rows. ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
chunk_size Chunk size used when converting the Polars source to NumPy arrays.
n_rows Total number of rows in the source used by the most recent fit.
### [chunk_size]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Chunk size used when converting the Polars source to NumPy arrays. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [chunk_size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} This is the `chunk_size` value passed to `__init__`: the number of rows per slice that `_lazyframe_to_dict` requests from `LazyFrame.iter_slices` while converting the collected frame into the `dict[str, numpy.ndarray]` consumed by fitting. ::: ### [n_rows]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Total number of rows in the source used by the most recent fit. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [n_rows]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Populated by `fit()` via `_count_lazy`, which evaluates `lf.select(pl.len())` with Polars' streaming engine before collecting the data. Remains `0` until `fit()` has been called at least once. ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
fit() Fit the GAM from a Polars source.
### [fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the GAM from a Polars source. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/polars_streaming.py#L205-L284){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python fit(data, *, smoothing_params=None, method="fREML", select=False, **kwargs) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Converts `data` to a Polars `LazyFrame`, collects it via Polars' streaming engine in `chunk_size`-row slices, and combines the result into `dict[str, numpy.ndarray]` before delegating to `~whittaker.bam.BigGAM`'s discretized fitting (see the class docstring for details on the discretization and cross-product accumulation). ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [polars.LazyFrame or polars.DataFrame or str or pathlib.Path]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The data source. A Polars `LazyFrame` is used as-is; a `DataFrame` is converted with `.lazy()`; a file path (string or `Path`) is scanned lazily based on its extension — `.parquet` (`scan_parquet`), `.csv` (`scan_csv`), `.ipc`/`.arrow` (`scan_ipc`), or `.ndjson`/`.jsonl` (`scan_ndjson`). Any other type or unrecognized extension raises `TypeError` or `ValueError` respectively. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [numpy.ndarray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observation (prior) weights, shape `(n,)`. Must be strictly positive. [smoothing_params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list of float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Fixed smoothing parameters `lambda_j`, one per smooth term, in formula order. If `None` (the default), smoothing parameters are selected automatically according to `method`. [method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["fREML"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Criterion used to select smoothing parameters when `smoothing_params` is `None`. One of `"fREML"` (default), `"REML"`, `"ML"`, or `"GCV"`. See `~whittaker.gam.GAM.fit` for a description of each criterion. [select]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, add an extra penalty on each smooth's null space so the term can be shrunk to exactly zero (double-penalty selection). Defaults to `False`. [**kwargs]{.doc-parameter-name} : Reserved for future keyword arguments; currently unused. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [PolarsGAM]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns `self` for method chaining, e.g. `model = PolarsGAM("y ~ s(x)").fit(data)`. :::
